heads.head: 046afadb037b16aba4b098170b3c80afcc9f2fc2
heads.title: Re-check approval when GitHub still lists the checks as pending after CI completes
heads.body:
Closes #86.

## Why

On #74, andabot's clean re-review posted "Approval waits for the checks". CI passed 13 seconds later, but the approval came only after CI was re-run four hours later. Workers Logs show what happened:

- `approval.decided` with trigger `checks_completed` → `review_in_flight`: the CI-completed event arrived while the review was posting.
- `approval.decided` with trigger `review` → `checks_pending`: the evaluation the review ran after posting read GitHub's check-runs list 17 seconds after GitHub had announced the run complete, and the job still showed as unfinished. GitHub had an Actions incident at the time.

GitHub sends one completion event per check suite, and that one had been used, so nothing evaluated again.

## What changes

- **`nextRecheck`** (`src/review/approval.ts`) decides whether an evaluation re-checks.
  - It re-checks only an evaluation triggered by `checks_completed`, or one of its own re-checks, and only when that evaluation failed or waited as `review_in_flight`, `checks_pending`, `checks_unknown`, `threads_unknown` or `workflow_unknown`.
  - The re-checks come 20 seconds, 1 minute and 5 minutes apart, and then stop.
  - Any other answer ends the chain, as does any other trigger: a review, a thread event and a command each leave the work to the completions still to come.
- **The object** pushes a durable Lifecycle job, `approval.recheck`, with one id per pull request. A later suite completion restarts the chain instead of adding a second one.
  - The new host `onJob` runs the job as an evaluation with the trigger `recheck`, and drops a job it can't read (`job.unreadable`).
  - The Pi harness's wake jobs belong to the harness, so they never reach the host's `onJob`, and the Lifecycle keeps the one alarm for both.
- **Logs:** `approval.recheck_scheduled` records the attempt, the delay and the delivery that started the chain.
- **`docs/design.md`** describes the re-check, the `recheck` trigger and the new log.

## Tests

`pnpm check` passes: lint, typecheck and 868 tests. The new `approval.test.ts` cases cover:
- the 20 s, 1 min and 5 min spacing, and the stop after the third re-check;
- each unsettled reason, and a failed evaluation;
- each final answer;
- every trigger other than `checks_completed` and `recheck`;
- the stored job's schema.

The object's wiring has no unit test, as elsewhere in the repo.

## Live check (not run yet)

GitHub's lag can't be forced, but the case where CI finishes while the review is posting can be. On a throwaway pull request, a small clean change gets its CI result in about 40 seconds, while its review takes about a minute. Expected logs:
1. `approval.decided` `checks_completed` → `review_in_flight`
2. `approval.recheck_scheduled` attempt 1
3. about 20 seconds later, `approval.decided` with trigger `recheck` finding the approval posted, or approving

A pull request whose CI finishes after its review should show no `recheck`.

issues.title: Re-check approval when GitHub still lists the checks as pending after CI completes
issues.body:
## What happened

On #74, andabot's re-review of `9568ce6` found nothing and posted "Approval waits for the checks" at 15:01:54Z on 22 Oct. CI passed, but no approval came until CI was re-run at 19:02Z.

From Workers Logs and GitHub:

- 15:01:41Z: CI's `check` job finished. At 15:01:52Z GitHub marked the run complete and sent `check_suite` completed.
- 15:01:54.7Z: the event reached the object while the review was publishing. `approval.decided` with trigger `checks_completed` waited with `review_in_flight`.
- 15:01:58.8Z: the evaluation the review starts after posting waited with `checks_pending`. GitHub's `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/check-runs` still listed the job as unfinished. A separate read at 15:02:09Z saw it `queued`. GitHub had "Incident with Actions Results" (degraded Actions) from 14:18 to 15:18Z.
- GitHub sends one completion event per check suite, and that one had been used, so nothing evaluated again.

## Cause

After the last CI-completed event, one evaluation decides, and a stale or failed read there is final. The review overlap isn't needed: any completion followed by a lagging read loses the approval the same way.

## Fix

When an evaluation that follows a CI-completed event can't settle, schedule a re-check through the Lifecycle job queue: about 20 seconds later, then 1 minute, then 5 minutes. "Can't settle" means the review is in flight, the checks read as pending, or a GitHub read fails (check runs, threads, `.andabot.yaml`, or the evaluation throws). Each re-check is an ordinary evaluation, logged with trigger `recheck`. The chain stops once the approval posts or the answer is final.

Trusting the event's own conclusion over the list was ruled out: it would count an earlier pass while CI is re-run on the same head.

## Done when

- Unit tests cover which triggers and outcomes re-check, the delays, the cap, and parsing a re-check job.
- After a deploy, normal approvals still post, and no re-check fires on a fresh read.

heads.head: 7c2b870063bc67970c316a0aac48fb3c00472a39
heads.title: Make the tar reader reject a cut-off or corrupt archive
heads.body:
Closes #94.

The tar reader from #88 now refuses an archive it can't trust, so the loader retries it once and then reports search unavailable, instead of keeping a partial or garbled snapshot.

- **A cut-off archive is truncated.** A stream that ends before the two zero blocks that close an archive throws `tar archive is truncated`, including at a block boundary and after a single zero block. A lone zero block followed by more entries is refused too. `git archive` always writes both blocks.
- **Each header's checksum is verified.** The sum counts the checksum field as spaces, per POSIX, and a mismatch throws. I left out the `ustar` magic check the issue mentions under gaps, since the checksum is what catches corruption and its "What to do" list doesn't ask for magic.
- **`parseSize` is strict.** It reads octal digits with optional leading spaces and trailing NULs or spaces only. Trailing junk, junk after the terminator, non-octal digits, an empty field and GNU base-256 sizes all throw.
- **Pax records are strict.** The length must be decimal, end inside the record, and land on a newline.

The loader test covers a gzipped archive cut at a block boundary: two tarball calls, then `SnapshotUnavailable` for the tarball step.

The skipped-entry test streams a 2 MiB entry past a 1,000-byte limit in 64 KiB chunks. It forces a garbage collection before each pull and checks, through weak references, that no earlier skipped chunk is still alive. The current reader keeps none. A reader that buffers the entry, by taking it instead of discarding it, keeps 31 of 32 and fails the test. The test stayed green over six runs.

I also ran the new reader over real GitHub tarballs. This repository's main reads all 150 files. React's main reads all 7,268, including its pax long paths.

The design doc's Repository search section says what the reader checks. `pnpm check` passes. Merging deploys nothing.

issues.title: Make the tar reader reject a cut-off or corrupt archive
issues.body:
The tar reader from #88 (`src/repository/tar.ts`) has gaps the task reviews recorded as minor:

- **A cut-off archive reads as complete.** A stream that ends on a 512-byte block boundary without the two zero-block terminator ends the loop like a finished archive. A truncated download can then become a partial snapshot with no error. The loader retries a failed download once, but this case doesn't fail.
- **No header checksum or `ustar` magic check.** A corrupt header is parsed as a file.
- **Loose size parsing.** `parseSize` accepts trailing junk.
- **Untested paths.** Nothing pins that a skipped entry isn't buffered, or the handling of malformed pax records and sizes.

## What to do

- Treat end of stream without the terminator as truncated, which makes the loader retry and then report search unavailable. Test it at a block boundary.
- Verify each header's checksum, and reject a header that fails it.
- Make `parseSize` strict.
- Add tests for malformed pax and size fields, and one showing a large skipped entry isn't held in memory.

## Done when

- The tests above pass under `pnpm check`.

heads.head: 89a836a4f23f69cd566a675752c58c881a8fddf3
heads.title: Show what each review cost in the summary comment
heads.body:
### What
- The summary footer says what the review cost, on the line under "Reviewed by", for example: `3 model calls · 61k in / 4.8k out tokens · ≈ 608 neurons ($0.007)`.
  - A model pi-ai has no price for shows `cost unknown`, or `+ unpriced <model>` next to the priced part.
  - Zero tokens shows `usage not reported`.
- `review.done` logs the same numbers: `calls`, `inputTokens`, `cachedTokens`, `outputTokens`, `models` (model:calls), `neurons` (to one decimal) and `usd`.
- `review.incomplete`, `review.failed` and `review.no_submission` log a failed review's spend as well.
- A log leaves `neurons` and `usd` out, rather than logging 0, when a price or the usage is missing.

Closes #32

### Why
- Nothing said what a review cost, and the Workers AI dashboard can't tie spend to one review. Comparing models on #2 needs it.

### Decisions (agreed in the session)
- **Prices come from pi-ai's registry,** not a table kept by hand. pi-ai generates `cloudflare-workers-ai.json` from Cloudflare's model catalog and pins it with the package. Its gpt-oss-120b prices match the pricing page. This departs from the issue's "price table in code", on purpose: a price change arrives with a pi-ai bump.
- **Neurons** are the dollars at Workers AI's $0.011 per 1,000.
- **"In" is the whole prompt,** cached tokens included. The neuron figure already reflects the cache discount, and `cachedTokens` is logged separately.
- **Measured once,** when the summary posts, and stored per model on `posted:<sha>`, so the footer and the log always agree and a future verify pass (#31) can add its own model without a new record format.

### How it measures
- Pi's `pi.usage` ledger only grows, across resets and the questions answered between reviews. So `pending` stores the ledger as it stood when the review started (`usageBefore`), and the spend is what it grew by when the summary posts. That includes the retry, failed attempts and compaction.
- The call count is the model's responses in the transcript since the review's reset.
- If the ledger can't be read, the review still posts, without the cost line, and logs `review.usage_unreadable`.
- A review already running when this deploys has no `usageBefore`, so it posts without the line.

### How to test
- `pnpm check`: lint, typecheck and 436 tests pass. The Workers dry-run build bundles.
- `test/cost.test.ts` covers:
  - the ledger delta, with cached input counted as input;
  - call counting;
  - clamping rounding error at zero;
  - the token, neuron and dollar formatting;
  - one call versus several;
  - several models;
  - unpriced, partly priced and unreported usage;
  - the log fields.
- `test/findings.test.ts`, `test/records.test.ts` and `test/flight.test.ts` cover the footer line, the stored spend and the stored baseline.
- Live, after merge and deploy: reopen #54 on GLM-5.3 Flash. Its footer should show the cost line, and `review.done` in Workers Logs should match it and the Workers AI dashboard for that window. Record the run on #2, then close #54 unmerged.

### High level code differences
- `src/review/cost.ts` (new): `usageTotals`, `callsByModel`, `spendSince`, `spendLine` and `spendFields`, with the `UsageTotals` and `ReviewSpend` schemas.
- `src/pull-request.ts`: records `usageBefore` in `pending`, works out the spend in `publishReview`, stores it on `posted:<sha>`, and adds it to the done and failure logs.
- `src/review/render.ts`: `renderSummaryComment` takes `spend` and renders the line.
- `src/records.ts` and `src/review/flight.ts`: optional `spend` on `PostedReview` and `usageBefore` on `StoredPending`.
- `docs/design.md`: the cost paragraph.

heads.head: 2d32ec31c694e1b644c5cda0ef3bddbfe153784a
heads.title: Give the reviewer the repository's own instructions, scoped to the paths a pull request touches
heads.body:
Closes #29.

Part A of slice 3 (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-skills-design.md`, section D, decided 21 Oct 2026, plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-21-repository-context.md`).

- **The repository's own instruction files reach the review.** One recursive trees call at the pull request's base commit finds `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `REVIEW.md`, `CODING_STANDARDS.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` at the root, `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` kept when their `applyTo` glob matches a changed file, and a nested `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` above any changed file. They render after the skill in the instructions as `## Repository standards`, most specific first, capped at 12,000 characters with a note naming what was cut. The base commit is the only source, so a pull request cannot change the rules it is reviewed by.
- **Cached per base commit.** The listing and the bodies are stored under `context:<baseSha>`; a later review of the same base loads only what is missing, at most 24 files per review with the root files first. A GitHub failure on one file is logged as `context.unreadable` and that file is skipped; a failure on the tree runs the review without standards. The stored record keeps only the entries that can matter, so a large repository still fits the storage limit.
- **Attribution.** The summary footer gains `Standards: `CLAUDE.md`, …` or `Standards: none`, and `review.start` logs `instructionFiles`, `standardsCut`, `instructionLoadsSkipped` and `treeTruncated`.
- **The review skill is version 6.** The Standards check now names the section, and `references/smells.md` says a repository rule is reported even when a linter enforces it, since the review cannot run the linter.
- **New dependency:** `minimatch` 10.2.6, pinned, for the `applyTo` globs; it bundles under `nodejs_compat`.

`pnpm check` passes with 518 tests. Merging deploys nothing. Deploy with `pnpm run deploy`; then the standards fixture (a pull request to this repository planting a comment and a type assertion, answer key on #2) runs on GLM-5.3 Flash, gpt-oss and Kimi.

issues.title: The summary command ignores path_filters: every changed file's patch goes to the model and gets a walkthrough row
issues.body:
Found by the whole-plan review of slice 3 (#29, #28, #75) on 23 Oct 2026.

`.andabot.yaml`'s `path_filters` leave files out of a review: no patch in the prompt, no walkthrough row, no finding (#28; `docs/design.md`'s `path_filters` bullet, `docs/setup.md` section 6). The `summary` command, which #74 brought in between Parts B and C, never applies them:

- `summary()` in `src/pull-request.ts` lists every changed file and puts every patch into the summary prompt.
- `postSummary` keeps a walkthrough row for every changed file in `reviewed`, and the next incremental review carries those rows through `mergeWalkthrough`.
- `renderSummaryRun` in `src/review/render.ts` leaves out the `_.andabot.yaml was ignored: …_` note a review's footer shows when the file is invalid or unreadable.

To see it: a base `.andabot.yaml` with `path_filters: ["!docs/**"]` and a pull request touching `docs/a.md` and `src/a.ts`. The review shows one patch and one row; `@andabot summary` sends both patches and writes both rows, spending tokens on exactly the paths the repository filtered out.

Fix: run `reviewableFiles(files, config.reviews.path_filters)` with the base's config before `askForSummary` and `postSummary`, pass the config's error to the summary footer, and change `docs/design.md`'s "its whole diff" under `summary` and `docs/setup.md`'s `path_filters` row to match. Both docs note the gap until then.

issues.body:
Seen on the repository-skills fixture (#77) on 23 Oct 2026: GLM-5.3 Flash's run logged `review.transcript` with `activate_skill:1 submit_review:2` over three turns, but a single `review.findings` (1 accepted, 0 rejected, 0 missing rows, `rejectionsReturned: false`). The first `submit_review` call never reached validation, and nothing says why. `submitReview` in `src/pull-request.ts` answers `no_review`, `not_in_flight`, a moved head and an already posted head with text for the model and no log event, and a call whose arguments fail the tool's schema leaves no andabot event either. The review posted on the second call, so nothing was lost, but the cause can't be told after the fact. The first suspect is #74's in-flight check, `submitStanding`, which refuses a call whose caller isn't the root conversation or whose operation isn't the pending review's.

Fix: log a `review.refused` event with the standing (`no_review`, `not_in_flight`, `head_moved`, `posted_already`), the head and the delivery id, and count refused calls in `review.transcript`.

issues.title: Tie the context cache write and the catalog restore to the review in flight
issues.body:
Found by the whole-plan review of slice 3 (#29, #28, #75) on 23 Oct 2026. Minor: it takes two reviews at different bases overlapping during the context load, or a tree failure at a new base, followed by a deploy or an eviction mid-review.

- `loadedContext` in `src/pull-request.ts` writes `context:<baseSha>` and sweeps the other `context:` records without checking that its review still owns `pending`. A review that has already been replaced can cache `context:<old>` and sweep `context:<new>`.

After a restart mid-review, Pi resumes the review with the old base's catalog; a tree failure at a new base leaves the old record in place with the same effect.

GitHub's tree lists a symlink (mode `120000`) with its link text's size and sha, while the contents API serves its target, so the skill caps passed a symlink to any file and the fingerprint never saw the target change. Now:

heads.title: Show what each review cost in the summary comment
heads.body:
### What
- The summary footer says what the review cost, on the line under "Reviewed by", for example: `3 model calls · 61k in / 4.8k out tokens · ≈ 608 neurons ($0.007)`.
  - A model pi-ai has no price for shows `cost unknown`, or `+ unpriced <model>` next to the priced part.
  - Zero tokens shows `usage not reported`.
- `review.done` logs the same numbers: `calls`, `inputTokens`, `cachedTokens`, `outputTokens`, `models` (model:calls), `neurons` (to one decimal) and `usd`.
- `review.incomplete`, `review.failed` and `review.no_submission` log a failed review's spend as well.
- A log leaves `neurons` and `usd` out, rather than logging 0, when a price or the usage is missing.

Closes #32

### Why
- Nothing said what a review cost, and the Workers AI dashboard can't tie spend to one review. Comparing models on #2 needs it.

### Decisions (agreed in the session)
- **Prices come from pi-ai's registry,** not a table kept by hand. pi-ai generates `cloudflare-workers-ai.json` from Cloudflare's model catalog and pins it with the package. Its gpt-oss-120b prices match the pricing page. This departs from the issue's "price table in code", on purpose: a price change arrives with a pi-ai bump.
- **Neurons** are the dollars at Workers AI's $0.011 per 1,000.
- **"In" is the whole prompt,** cached tokens included. The neuron figure already reflects the cache discount, and `cachedTokens` is logged separately.
- **Measured once,** when the summary posts, and stored per model on `posted:<sha>`, so the footer and the log always agree and a future verify pass (#31) can add its own model without a new record format.

### How it measures
- Pi's `pi.usage` ledger only grows, across resets and the questions answered between reviews. So `pending` stores the ledger as it stood when the review started (`usageBefore`), and the spend is what it grew by when the summary posts. That includes the retry, failed attempts and compaction.
- The call count is the model's responses in the transcript since the review's reset.
- If the ledger can't be read, the review still posts, without the cost line, and logs `review.usage_unreadable`.
- A review already running when this deploys has no `usageBefore`, so it posts without the line.

### How to test
- `pnpm check`: lint, typecheck and 436 tests pass. The Workers dry-run build bundles.
- `test/cost.test.ts` covers:
  - the ledger delta, with cached input counted as input;
  - call counting;
  - clamping rounding error at zero;
  - the token, neuron and dollar formatting;
  - one call versus several;
  - several models;
  - unpriced, partly priced and unreported usage;
  - the log fields.
- `test/findings.test.ts`, `test/records.test.ts` and `test/flight.test.ts` cover the footer line, the stored spend and the stored baseline.
- Live, after merge and deploy: reopen #54 on GLM-5.3 Flash. Its footer should show the cost line, and `review.done` in Workers Logs should match it and the Workers AI dashboard for that window. Record the run on #2, then close #54 unmerged.

### High level code differences
- `src/review/cost.ts` (new): `usageTotals`, `callsByModel`, `spendSince`, `spendLine` and `spendFields`, with the `UsageTotals` and `ReviewSpend` schemas.
- `src/pull-request.ts`: records `usageBefore` in `pending`, works out the spend in `publishReview`, stores it on `posted:<sha>`, and adds it to the done and failure logs.
- `src/review/render.ts`: `renderSummaryComment` takes `spend` and renders the line.
- `src/records.ts` and `src/review/flight.ts`: optional `spend` on `PostedReview` and `usageBefore` on `StoredPending`.
- `docs/design.md`: the cost paragraph.

heads.head: d320027d229ae367e6027ec571af591b2ff71f58
heads.title: Let the reviewer grep the repository at the pull request's head
heads.body:
Closes #30.

The review model can now search the pull request's head. It gets `grep(pattern, glob?, path?)` and `tree(path?, depth?)` over every text file at the commit under review, so it can find the callers of a changed signature that live outside the diff. Questions asked in a thread get the same tools. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-repository-search-design.md` is the design; `docs/design.md`'s Repository search section says how it works now.

## What it does

- **The snapshot.** The first `grep` or `tree` call of a review, or of a question, loads the head's text files. It streams the tarball through `DecompressionStream` into a tar reader written for this, with no new dependency for this part. It keeps each regular file of 1 MB or less that has no NUL byte in its first 8 KB, and stores them in the object's SQLite (`snapshot_files`, `snapshot_left_out`, `snapshot_meta`).
- **What GitHub's archive leaves out.** Paths marked `export-ignore` are missing from the tarball. The loader reads the recursive tree and fills them back in through GraphQL batches, up to 500 files.
- **What stays out.** Large, binary, LFS, submodule and symlink files stay out, and the tools name them by reason instead of saying "no match".
- **Caps.** A snapshot holds at most 50,000 files or 400 MB.
- **Cleanup.** The snapshot is dropped when the review or answer that loaded it ends. A stale leftover is dropped at the start of the next `review()` or `comment()`. Overlapping runs share one load, and the drop waits for the last of them.
- **grep runs on `re2js` 2.9.0, a linear-time engine.** V8's backtracking took more than 90 s on patterns like `(.\w?)*zzz` over react, and no set of refusal rules kept up with it.
  - **Work budget.** A per-call budget charges what `re2js` actually does: DFA states built, OnePass steps for `^`-anchored patterns, prefilter scans past the free ones, and a fixed cost per line. A pattern built to defeat the engine therefore stops early with a note, while ordinary patterns and literals still cover the whole 400 MB snapshot cap.
  - **Worst case.** The worst crafted case measured is about 15 s per call, on Node 22, not workerd.
- **Limits.** `limits.cpu_ms` is now 300,000, the maximum. A review shares 40 `grep`/`tree` calls between the review and any questions.
- **Tool order and skill.** The tools are `read_file`, `list_changed_files`, `get_issue`, `grep`, `tree` and `submit_review`. The review skill (now v8) tells the model to grep for callers when a signature, export or type changes, and to read a function before writing a failure scenario that depends on it.
- **Logs.**
  - The loader logs `snapshot.loaded`, `.failed`, `.dropped`, `.drop_failed` and `.gap_fill_failed`.
  - `review.done` adds `greps` and `trees`.

## Live checks (23 Oct 2026, on GLM-5.3 Flash)

- **This repository, #82.** A throwaway change to `answerPrompt`'s signature, leaving its caller unchanged. The review:
  - ran `grep` 3 times;
  - posted a blocking finding naming `src/pull-request.ts:1796` and the test callers;
  - cost 896 neurons ($0.010).

  `snapshot.loaded` reported 131 files and 1.3 MB.
- **A private, large repository, `ItsAndrewM/andabot-search-fixture#1`.** This is react at a pinned commit, plus an `export-ignore` directory that holds the only caller of the function the change touches.
  - The snapshot loaded with the installation token: 7,214 files and 37.6 MB, with `gapFilled=1`.
  - The load took about 1.8 s of CPU.
  - The blocking finding names `andabot-fixture/needle-caller.js:4`, which the review could only see through the gap fill.
  - The review cost 151 neurons.
- **Also on that build.** #84 was reviewed twice on it, using `grep` and `tree`; its snapshot loaded and dropped cleanly.

`pnpm check`: 42 files, 1,028 tests.

## Rulings I made

Andrew decided the tarball, the private-repository live check, re2js and the work budget. These calls are mine, each with what it costs if it's wrong:

- **The charge's numbers come from measurements on Node 22 on Apple silicon:** `MAX_SEARCH_WORK = 750,000,000`, `LINE_UNITS = 16`, the OnePass rate of program size per character, one free Aho–Corasick scan and three free substring scans. *If wrong:* the real bound on workerd differs from about 15 s, still under the 300 s `cpu_ms`.
- **OnePass and the prefilter are read through re2js internals.** OnePass uses the declared `re2Input.onepass` and `dfa.stateCount`/`startStates`. The prefilter uses its undeclared `cost`/`allExact`/`subs`, behind a TypeBox schema. re2js is pinned exactly, and table tests fail if an upgrade changes these. *If wrong:* a re2js upgrade needs those tests' attention.
- **Literals are overcharged up to about 100×, because nothing shows when the prefilter answered.** *If wrong:* nothing, unless the snapshot cap rises past about 700 MB.
- **A `^`-anchored pattern is charged at the OnePass rate even when it gives up at the first character.** *If wrong:* an anchored search on a vscode-size repository may need a path or glob.
- **The budget is per call, not per review.** *If wrong:* a model that repeats a crafted pattern many times in one event could approach `cpu_ms`. That's a follow-up.
- **The grep line cap stays at 500 characters, with its note.** *If wrong:* matches past column 500 are missed, minified lines mostly.
- **grep, tree and read_file ignore `.andabot.yaml`'s path filters.** Filters say what isn't reviewed, not what can't be read. *If wrong:* search returns hits in generated files.
- **Overlapping runs.** A count of active runs drops the snapshot only when it reaches 0. grep and tree re-check the record before scanning, and a stale snapshot is dropped at the start of `review()` and `comment()`. *If wrong:* a snapshot lives until the last overlapping run ends, or a resumed run reloads.
- **A failed gap-fill batch marks only its own paths `unreadable`, and the snapshot still finishes.** Write batches are 200 files or 8 MB. *If wrong:* one more left-out reason, and more SQL calls.
- **`tree` lists paths without reading contents, through `SnapshotFiles.paths()`.** *If wrong:* one more interface method.
- **grep and tree aren't `replay: "safe"`, so a scan that resets the object isn't rerun.** *If wrong:* an interrupted call has to be retried by the model.
- **The never-produced `unlisted` reason was removed.** A truncated tree sets `treeTruncated` instead, and the tools then say the snapshot is incomplete. *If wrong:* nothing.
- **The stale-snapshot drop runs before #27's pause gate.** It only clears leftovers. *If wrong:* nothing.
- **The review skill is v8, since this branch and main each moved it from 6 to 7.** *If wrong:* nothing.

## Follow-ups I'd open

- Bound grep's work per review as well as per call.
- Drop the snapshot on the `closed` event, too.
- Fix the tar reader's minor gaps:
  - a stream ending on a block boundary without the zero-block terminator reads as complete;
  - no checksum or `ustar` magic check.
- Add the missing test coverage:
  - tool wrappers' argument pass-through;
  - snapshot-vs-API parity for the 60k cap.
- Fix the small search gaps:
  - `$` and `\b` can match at the 500-character cut;
  - left-out examples aren't length-capped against the 12,000-character answer;
  - a superseded review's grep can briefly search the new head.
- Compare the review footer's cost with and without the tools on the same pull request. The spec's "done when" asks for this, and #82's 896 neurons is the number to compare.

heads.head: d35a04eb338847ed11efb2d6edbf100102a5db6b
heads.title: Check stored records, move liveness into decideFlight, and end runs after releasing them
heads.body:
### What
- Every stored record the object reads with `get<T>` is now parsed with TypeBox: the `posted:<sha>` record, `summaryCommentId`, the pull request `key` and the cached installation `token`.
- `decideFlight` now decides liveness itself (a listed operation, or a start inside the two-minute grace), and `ownsOperation` lives beside it, both with tests. The start of 0 that an old record migrates to is named, with a test that says why.
- A run that finds its head posted by an earlier run completes with that review's verdict and counts in its title, since `posted:` records now store the counts. Records from before this change show the verdict alone.
- Every review exit now releases `pending` before completing its own run (`endOwnRun`), so a newer head that reads the record during that GitHub call can't mark a finished run "Superseded". The retry re-checks for replacement right before its prompt, as the first prompt already does.
- A review that finds itself replaced logs `review.superseded` only when the newer review is of another head, and `review.withdrawn` when it's of the same head.
- Tidy-ups: one shared `shortSha` (there were three), `PendingReview` derived from `StoredPending`, the unread `reason` on the skip decision removed, a test that `check_run` `created` is ignored, and `docs/setup.md`'s rollout steps in the order the code runs them.

### Why
- Closes #21, the follow-ups from the review of #16. Its two "For the live checks on #8" questions were answered on #8: the fallback summary comment does appear for a model that doesn't exist, and the check run id in `pending` behaves as #8 asked.
- Not done: #21 item 6 also asked for the summary comment's Markdown in the "posted earlier" run. That run's summary is one line, and Details opens the summary comment. Copying the full text would mean storing up to 64 KB per head, or another GitHub call.

### How to test
1. `pnpm check`: lint, typecheck and 336 tests pass. New or changed tests:
   - `test/records.test.ts`: the key, the comment id, and posted records with and without counts.
   - `test/flight.test.ts`: liveness and the grace boundary, `ownsOperation`, `replacedExit`, and the migrated start.
   - `test/check.test.ts`: `postedEarlierCheckRun`, and titles from counts.
   - `test/app-auth.test.ts`: the cached token.
   - `test/route.test.ts`: `check_run` `created`.
2. Live, after a deploy (`pull-request.ts` has no unit tests, so the release order needs this):
   - An ordinary review completes its run, and a second review of the same head starts normally afterwards.
   - Two pushes a few seconds apart: the first head's run reads "Superseded by …", the second head's run completes with its verdict, and Workers Logs show `review.superseded` for the first.

### High level code differences

issues.title: Follow-ups from the review of #16: check stored records, fix the rollout order, test the ignored check events
issues.body:
A two-axis review of #16 (Standards and Spec, head `2b20603` against main at `9768afa`) found nothing that posts a wrong review or loses data. #16 merged without the items below. They're small, and every one was checked against the code.

## Standards

1. **Unchecked stored reads.** `CLAUDE.md` asks for stored JSON to be parsed with TypeBox and `Value.Check`.
   - `summaryCommentUrl()` reads `storage.get<number>("summaryCommentId")` without a check, as `upsertSummary` already did.
   - `posted:<sha>` is read with `storage.get<PostedReview>` without a check. #16 now feeds its `event` to `VERDICT_LABEL[event]` through `completeAsPostedEarlier`. A `StoredPosted` schema like `StoredPending` would cover both reads.
2. **A default with no stated reason.** `migratePending` defaults `started` to 0, so that a record written before #16 falls outside the grace and only the harness listing can keep it live. No name, test title or `docs/design.md` line says so.
3. **Rollout order in `docs/setup.md`.** Step 3 opens the check run before step 4 fetches the PR and its files. The code fetches both first, then opens the run.

## Spec (#8)

4. `check_run` `created` is ignored in `src/route.ts` but has no test. #8's "Done when" lists the ignored check events.
5. Liveness, `operations.length > 0 || withinGrace(pending)`, is computed outside `decideFlight` and has no test. #8 asked for the start, skip or abort decision as a pure function with tests.
6. `completeAsPostedEarlier` completes the run with only the verdict as its title. The success row in #8 asks for the non-zero counts and the summary comment's Markdown.

## Races (cosmetic; nothing wrong is posted)

7. Each review completes its own run before it releases `pending`. A newer head that reads `pending` during that update marks the same run as superseded. Whichever update lands last wins, so a run that just completed can end as "Superseded by …".
8. The retry still has the window that `2b20603` narrowed for the first prompt. A newer head that arrives between `askAgain`'s `replaced()` check and the retry prompt reaching the harness finds nothing to abort. The old retry then runs to the end, and its submit is refused.

## Judgement calls

- `PendingReview` and `StoredPending` list the same fields. Derive one from the other.
- `shortSha` in `src/review/check.ts` repeats `short` in `src/pull-request.ts`.
- Nothing reads the `skip` decision's `reason` field.
- `replaced()` logs `review.superseded` even when a same-head review is replaced as dead.
- `ownsOperation` and `withinGrace` read only `PendingReview`. In `src/review/flight.ts` they could be unit-tested.

## For the live checks on #8

- With a `REVIEW_MODEL` that doesn't exist, the prompt may throw instead of returning `unanswered`. If it throws, the catch in `runReview` fails the run but writes no fallback summary comment, which one of #8's "Done when" items expects.
- For Andrew to sign off: the check run id lives in the single `pending` record, not in a run record keyed by head sha as #8 asked. It behaves the same under #8's rules.

heads.body:
Closes #28.

Part B of slice 3 (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-skills-design.md`, section D, plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-21-repository-context.md`).

- **`.andabot.yaml` at the base commit.** Parsed with `yaml` and a TypeBox schema, cached per base commit under `config:<baseSha>`. A missing file gives the defaults; an invalid one gives the defaults and a note in the summary comment naming the first problem; an unreadable one gives the defaults for that review only, logged as `config.unreadable`. A pull request cannot change the rules it is reviewed by.
- **The settings under `reviews`.** `auto` (`false` means pushes start no review and only commands do), `drafts` (the router now forwards drafts and the object decides), `base_branches` (an exact list), `ignore_title_keywords`, `request_changes_workflow` (overrides the Worker var in both the review's event and the approval evaluation), `path_filters` (`!`-prefixed globs that join the generated-file filter for the prompt and the walkthrough rows) and `path_instructions` (rendered first under `## Repository standards` when their glob matches a changed file). `model` is accepted and ignored until the verify pass. A skipped push logs `review.skip` with the setting's name and opens no check run.
- **Approval and drafts.** The approval evaluation from #25 runs under the workflow the review ran under, stored on the last-review record; when an older record lacks it and the config cannot be read, the evaluation waits rather than guessing. A draft reviewed under `drafts: true` and later marked ready gets its waiting approval when the ready-for-review push is skipped as already reviewed. A finding on a filtered file is rejected as unfounded and holds no approval back; a pull request whose every file is filtered is skipped.
- **Docs.** `docs/setup.md` documents the file with every setting and its default; `docs/design.md`'s configuration section, events table and state list match. Merged with main after #67, so the 👀 text says a review follows unless the file skips it.

issues.title: Read an optional .andabot.yaml for per-repository review settings
issues.body:
Every repository gets the same settings today, from Worker vars: `REVIEW_MODEL` and `REQUEST_CHANGES_WORKFLOW`. `docs/design.md` plans an optional `.andabot.yaml`:

```yaml
reviews:
  auto: true
  drafts: false
  base_branches: ["main"]
  ignore_title_keywords: ["WIP"]
  request_changes_workflow: true
  path_instructions: [...]
  path_filters: ["!pnpm-lock.yaml", "!**/*.snap"]
model:
  draft: "..."
  verify: "..."
```

The design reads the file from the PR head, but the skills design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-skills-design.md`, section D) trusts the base commit only, so that a pull request can't change the rules it is reviewed by. Its open question about a missing file ("default branch, then built-in defaults") settles the same way.

## What to do

1. **Read** `.andabot.yaml` from the PR's base commit, falling back to built-in defaults. Parse it with a pinned, Workers-compatible YAML library and validate it with TypeBox. When it's invalid, use the defaults and say so in the summary comment.
2. **Apply:**
   - `auto` decides whether pushes review or only commands do;
   - `drafts`, `base_branches` and `ignore_title_keywords` filter in the router or the object;
   - `request_changes_workflow` overrides the Worker var per repository;
   - `path_filters` joins `isGenerated`.
3. **Not here:** `path_instructions` is #29, and `model.draft` and `model.verify` go with the verify pass (#31).
4. **Docs.** Change `docs/design.md`'s configuration section to read from the base commit and give the reason, and add the file to `docs/setup.md`.

## Done when

- Unit tests cover parsing, validation failures, the defaults, and each setting's effect.
- On a repository with `auto: false`, a push starts no review, and `@andabot review` still does.

heads.title: Hold the retry to a submit_review call or the review as JSON (#18)
heads.body:
Addresses #18; it closes once a review that ends in prose is posted from the retry on this build.

On #16, gpt-oss-120b wrote its review as Markdown. When asked again, it answered "Review submitted." without calling `submit_review`, so #16 looked reviewed but had no review. #18 proposed forcing the call with `tool_choice` on the retry. Direct calls to gpt-oss-120b on Workers AI show that can't work: the vLLM front end accepts a named or `"required"` choice and then ignores it. With a prompt that forbade tools, forced runs called the tool 0 of 6 times. A `json_schema` `response_format` is enforced, even with tools in the request. The findings are on #18.

- **The retry is held to JSON.** When the latest message is the retry prompt, `withForcedResubmission` gives the request `ReviewSubmission` as its `response_format`. It goes through pi-ai's `samplingParams`, which keeps the code free of casts, since pi-ai's `toolChoice` type is only `"auto" | "none"`. The check reads only the transcript, so it still works after a Durable Object restart. Review requests, tool-result turns and chat answers are left alone.
- **The host posts JSON the retry ends in.** It goes through the same `parseWrittenReview` → `postReview` path as JSON from the first run. `review.done` logs it as `source: "retry_text"`, and a refusal logs `review.retry_text_refused`.
- **A review needs at least one walkthrough entry.** Held to JSON and pressed to confirm, the model wrote "Review submitted." as the summary of an approval with no walkthrough and no findings in 2 of 3 runs. That would have posted an approval nobody made. With `minItems: 1`, the host refuses that empty review, and in 4 of 4 runs under the same pressure the model wrote out its real review. This also applies to normal `submit_review` calls: an empty walkthrough now comes back to the model as a validation error.
- **The system prompt's closing line now reads** "Only a submit_review call posts the review; after it reports that it posted, reply in one short sentence."

`pnpm check` passes (139 tests). The unit tests cover the wrapper (it holds the retry, frees the request once `submit_review` has a result, and leaves review and chat requests alone), the prompt wording, and the refusal of the empty review. `postedRetryText` has no unit test, because `pull-request.ts` has no test harness. It needs the live run below.

Merging deploys nothing. Deploy with `pnpm run deploy`, then watch Workers Logs for `review.done` with `source: "retry_text"`, or `review.retry_text_refused`, on the next review that ends in prose.

issues.title: Stop the model from claiming a review was submitted without calling submit_review
issues.body:
andabot's review of #16 at `17c6a30` (build `711e4eee`, gpt-oss-120b) never posted. Workers Logs show what happened:

- `review.start`: 14 files and a prompt of 74,953 characters.
- No `review.findings` event follows, so the model never called `submit_review`. It wrote the review as Markdown prose: a summary, a walkthrough, five findings and a `request_changes` verdict.
- The host asked once more. The model answered "Review submitted." without calling the tool. The log shows `review.no_submission` with `wrote: "prose"` and `retryText: "Review submitted."`, after 50 s.

The summary comment kept the prose as its note. So #16 looks as if andabot requested changes, but it has no review at all. #6 and #7 were the same failure: the model writing its review out as text. #6's fallback can post such a review only when the text is JSON.

## Why it happens

- Nothing forces the tool. The review prompt and the retry are both plain requests, and the model can answer either with text.
- The system prompt ends with "After submit_review reports that it posted, reply in one short sentence." "Review submitted." reads like that sentence, written without the call it should follow.

## What to do

1. **Force the call on the retry.** The only valid answer to the retry is a `submit_review` call. `src/models.ts` already wraps the provider's `streamSimple` to set `maxTokens`, so the same wrapper can set `toolChoice` on the retry's requests only. The Agents SDK's Workers AI adapter (`toolChoiceOf` in `agents/models/pi-ai`) passes `"required"` and `{ name }` through to Workers AI's `tool_choice`.
2. **Settle two things first:**
   - pi-ai 1.3.0 declares `toolChoice` as `"auto" | "none"`, narrower than the adapter accepts. Passing `{ name: "submit_review" }` needs a typed route that isn't a cast, since `CLAUDE.md` bans casts.
   - Whether gpt-oss-120b on Workers AI honors `tool_choice`. One forced call against the model settles it.
3. **Reword the closing line** so that a short sentence can't stand in for the call. For example: "Only a submit_review call posts the review; after it reports that it posted, reply in one short sentence."

## Done when

- A unit test shows the wrapper forces `submit_review` on the retry's requests and leaves review and chat requests alone.
- A review that ends in prose is posted from the forced retry. If Workers AI ignores `tool_choice`, this issue records that and names the next option.
